content: Arbitrary ordering of unordered collections in recurrent networks (RNN). Most data-to-text systems use RNNs as encoders (such as GRUs or LSTMs), these architectures have however some limitations. Indeed, they require in practice their input to be fed sequentially. This way of encoding unordered sequences (i.e. collections of entities) implicitly assumes an arbitrary order within the collection which, as demonstrated by Vinyals et al. BIBREF20, significantly impacts the learning performance.
